questions.question_text: The partial differential equation formed by eliminating arbitrary constant is $z=(x+a)(y+b)$.
questions.answer: Differentiation gives $p=y+b$ and $q=x+a$, hence $z=pq$.

questions.question_text: The general integral of $z=xp+yq$ is
questions.answer: The characteristic equations are $dx/x=dy/y=dz/z$, giving the general integral $\Phi(x/y,y/z)=0$. The printed option B has a plus sign instead of a comma and describes only a restricted family, so no printed option gives the general integral.

questions.question_text: The particular integral of $(D^3-2D^2D\prime)z=e^{x+2y}$ is
questions.answer: Substituting $(D,D\prime)=(1,2)$ gives $1-4=-3$, so the particular integral is $-e^{x+2y}/3$.

questions.question_text: Solve $(D^3-7DD\prime^2-6D\prime^3)z=0$.
questions.answer: $m^3-7m-6=(m+1)(m+2)(m-3)$; each factor $D-mD\prime$ contributes an arbitrary function of $y+mx$.

questions.question_text: $\tan x$ is a periodic function with period
questions.answer: $\tan(x+\pi)=\tan x$ wherever defined; its fundamental period is $\pi$.

questions.question_text: The constant $a_0$ of the Fourier series for the function $f(x)=k$, $0\leq x\leq 2\pi$ is
questions.answer: With the series convention $a_0/2+\sum(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx)$, $a_0=\pi^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}k\,dx=2k$.

questions.question_text: The RMS value of $f(x)$ in $a\leq x\leq b$ is
questions.answer: Take the mean of $f^2$ over the interval and then its nonnegative square root.

questions.question_text: For half range cosine series of $f(x)=\cos x$ in $(0,\pi)$ the value of $a_0$ is
questions.answer: $a_0=(2/\pi)\int_0^\pi\cos x\,dx=0$.

questions.question_text: How many initial and boundary conditions are required to solve $\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2}=a^2\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}$?
questions.answer: For a finite string one normally specifies initial displacement and velocity and one boundary condition at each end: four conditions.

questions.answer: Thermal diffusivity is $\alpha^2=k/(\rho c)$, where $k$ is conductivity, $\rho$ density and $c$ specific heat.

questions.answer: At steady state $u_{xx}=0$. Using $u(0)=30$ and $u(l)=40$ gives $u=30+10x/l$.

questions.question_text: The Fourier cosine transform of $e^{-ax}$ is
questions.answer: For $a>0$, $F_c(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\int_0^\infty e^{-ax}\cos(sx)\,dx=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,a/(a^2+s^2)$.

questions.question_text: $F[f(x)\cos ax]=$
questions.answer: Use $\cos ax=(e^{iax}+e^{-iax})/2$ and the frequency-shift property.

questions.question_text: $F[e^{iax}f(x)]=$
questions.answer: With the convention $F(s)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)e^{-isx}\,dx$, combining exponentials gives $F(s-a)$. The sign reverses under the opposite Fourier convention.
For the unnormalized Fourier transform and standard convolution, the convolution theorem gives $F(s)G(s)$. Other normalizations introduce a constant factor.

questions.question_text: $Z\left[\sin\frac{n\pi}{2}\right]=$
questions.answer: $Z\{\sin n\theta\}=z\sin\theta/(z^2-2z\cos\theta+1)$; set $\theta=\pi/2$.

questions.question_text: Find $Z\left[1/7^n\right]$.
questions.answer: The geometric series gives $Z\{(1/7)^n\}=z/(z-1/7)=7z/(7z-1)$ for $|z|>1/7$.
$e^{1/z}=\sum_{n=0}^\infty z^{-n}/n!$, so the sequence is $1/n!$.

questions.question_text: Find $Z^{-1}\left[\frac{z}{(z-1)^2}\right]$.
Find the general solution $x(z^2-y^2)p+y(x^2-z^2)q=z(y^2-x^2)$.
questions.answer: The characteristic equations are $\frac{dx}{x(z^2-y^2)}=\frac{dy}{y(x^2-z^2)}=\frac{dz}{z(y^2-x^2)}$. Along them, $d(x^2+y^2+z^2)=0$ and $d(xyz)=0$. Thus the general integral is $\Phi(x^2+y^2+z^2,xyz)=0$, for arbitrary $\Phi$.

questions.question_text: Solve $(D^2-2DD\prime)z=x^3y+e^{2x}$.
questions.answer: The complementary function of $D(D-2D\prime)$ is $f(y)+g(y+2x)$. A polynomial particular integral is $x^5y/20+x^6/60$, because applying $D^2-2DD\prime$ yields $x^3y$; the exponential particular integral is $e^{2x}/4$. Hence $z=f(y)+g(y+2x)+x^5y/20+x^6/60+e^{2x}/4$.

questions.question_text: Expand $f(x)=(x-1)^2$ in $0<x<1$ in a Fourier sine series.
questions.answer: With $b_n=2\int_0^1(1-x)^2\sin(n\pi x)\,dx$, integration by parts gives $b_n=\frac{2}{n\pi}+\frac{4((-1)^n-1)}{n^3\pi^3}$. Therefore $(x-1)^2=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left[\frac{2}{n\pi}+\frac{4((-1)^n-1)}{n^3\pi^3}\right]\sin(n\pi x)$ for $0<x<1$.

questions.question_text: Express $f(x)=x(\pi-x)$, $0<x<\pi$, as a Fourier sine series.
questions.answer: $b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi x(\pi-x)\sin(nx)\,dx=\frac{4(1-(-1)^n)}{\pi n^3}$. Consequently $x(\pi-x)=\frac{8}{\pi}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{\sin((2j+1)x)}{(2j+1)^3}$.

questions.question_text: A tightly stretched string has its ends fixed at $x=0$ and $x=l$. Initially the string is in the form $y=kx(l-x)$, where $k$ is a constant, and then released form rest. Find the displacement at any point $x$ and any time $t>0$.
questions.answer: Let $c$ be the wave speed. The fixed-end wave solution is $y=\sum_{n\ge1}(A_n\cos(n\pi ct/l)+B_n\sin(n\pi ct/l))\sin(n\pi x/l)$. Release from rest gives $B_n=0$. From the initial shape, $A_n=\frac{2k}{l}\int_0^l x(l-x)\sin(n\pi x/l)\,dx=\frac{4kl^2(1-(-1)^n)}{n^3\pi^3}$. Thus $y=\frac{8kl^2}{\pi^3}\sum_{j=0}^\infty\frac{\sin((2j+1)\pi x/l)\cos((2j+1)\pi ct/l)}{(2j+1)^3}$.

questions.question_text: A rod of length $l$ has its end A and B kept at $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $100^\circ\mathrm{C}$ until steady state conditions prevail. If the temperature at B is reduced suddenly to $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and kept so while that of A is maintained, find the temperature $u(x,t)$ at a distance $x$ from A and at time $t$.
questions.answer: Let $\alpha^2$ be the thermal diffusivity. Before cooling, the steady temperature is $u(x,0)=100x/l$. Afterward $u(0,t)=u(l,t)=0$ and $u_t=\alpha^2u_{xx}$. Separation of variables gives $u=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n\sin(n\pi x/l)e^{-\alpha^2n^2\pi^2t/l^2}$, with $b_n=(2/l)\int_0^l(100x/l)\sin(n\pi x/l)\,dx=200(-1)^{n+1}/(n\pi)$. Substitute these coefficients into the series.

questions.question_text: Find $F_s(e^{-ax})$ and $F_c(e^{-ax})$ and hence derive the inversion formula.
questions.answer: For $a>0$ and $F_s(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\int_0^\infty f(x)\sin(sx)\,dx$, $F_c(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\int_0^\infty f(x)\cos(sx)\,dx$, direct integration yields $F_s(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,s/(a^2+s^2)$ and $F_c(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,a/(a^2+s^2)$. Fourier sine and cosine inversion give, for $x>0$, $e^{-ax}=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{s\sin(sx)}{a^2+s^2}\,ds=\frac{2a}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{\cos(sx)}{a^2+s^2}\,ds$.

questions.question_text: Prove that $e^{-x^2/2}$ is self-reciprocal under Fourier transforms.
questions.answer: Use the symmetric convention $F(s)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^\infty f(x)e^{-isx}\,dx$. Let $I(s)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2/2}e^{-isx}\,dx$. Integration by parts gives $I\prime(s)=-sI(s)$, and the Gaussian integral gives $I(0)=\sqrt{2\pi}$. Thus $I(s)=\sqrt{2\pi}e^{-s^2/2}$ and $F(s)=e^{-s^2/2}$, the same function.

questions.question_text: Find the inverse z-transform of $\frac{1+2z^{-1}}{1-z^{-1}}$ by long division method.
questions.answer: Long division in $z^{-1}$ gives $1+3z^{-1}+3z^{-2}+3z^{-3}+\cdots$ for $|z|>1$. Therefore $x_0=1$ and $x_n=3$ for $n\ge1$.

questions.question_text: Find the inverse z-transform of $\frac{4z^2-12z}{z^3-3z+2}$ by partial fraction method.
questions.answer: $z^3-3z+2=(z-1)^2(z+2)$. Decomposition in standard transform pairs gives $X(z)=\frac{20}{9}\frac{z}{z-1}-\frac{8}{3}\frac{z}{(z-1)^2}-\frac{20}{9}\frac{z}{z+2}$. For the unilateral transform, $x_n=\frac{20}{9}-\frac{8n}{3}-\frac{20}{9}(-2)^n$, $n\ge0$, with $|z|>2$.

questions.question_text: Solve $y_{n+2}-7y_{n+1}+12y_n=2^n$, given $y_0=0$, $y_1=0$ using Z transform method.
questions.answer: With $Y(z)=Z\{y_n\}$ and the stated initial values, $(z^2-7z+12)Y(z)=z/(z-2)$. Hence $Y=\frac{z}{(z-2)(z-3)(z-4)}=\frac12\frac{z}{z-2}-\frac{z}{z-3}+\frac12\frac{z}{z-4}$. Taking inverse transforms yields $y_n=\frac12 2^n-3^n+\frac12 4^n$, $n\ge0$.

questions.question_text: Compute first three harmonics of the half-range cosine series of $y=f(x)$ from: $\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}x&0&1&2&3&4&5\\\hline f(x)&4&8&15&7&6&2\end{array}$.
questions.answer: The data alone do not uniquely determine the continuous Fourier coefficients; using the standard trapezoidal harmonic analysis on $0\le x\le5$, $a_n\approx\frac25[\frac12 f(0)+\sum_{j=1}^4f(j)\cos(n\pi j/5)+\frac12f(5)(-1)^n]$. This gives $a_0=15.6$, $a_1=\sqrt5-0.2\approx2.0361$, $a_2=-(12+4\sqrt5)/5\approx-4.1889$, and $a_3=-\sqrt5-0.2\approx-2.4361$. Thus the estimated series through three harmonics is $7.8+2.0361\cos(\pi x/5)-4.1889\cos(2\pi x/5)-2.4361\cos(3\pi x/5)$.
